I built an AI tool to redesign my portfolio.

Then I caught its own taste-judge scoring a nearly-blank page HIGHER than a clean one. It was rewarding emptiness.

Here's how I caught it — and proved the fix blind. 🧵

Its original judge scored looks on 6 legibility rules — hierarchy, spacing, alignment.

But a page can be flawlessly legible and say nothing. So it scored a nearly-empty draft 87.1 — ABOVE a clean page at 83.1.

Top marks for doing the least.

So I rebuilt the judge: 11 dimensions, 5 of them STRUCTURAL — depth, rhythm, hierarchy-contrast, distinctiveness.

The trick is a band that PEAKS in the middle. You can't max it by being empty OR by being cluttered. Genuinely-composed design is what scores high.

Then I tested the fix honestly: ran the new judge BLIND on 6 real screenshots — no labels, no hints.

It scored my old generic site 4.8, and three new redesigns 7.7 — and sorted all six into the right buckets. 6 for 6.

Same résumé. Before 4.8, after 7.7 — on the same ruler.

Three redesigns, three directions (editorial / terminal / Swiss), all proven better — not just "looks different."

It's open source — a Claude Code skill that validates every UI change with objective metrics AND a vision-judge, and reverts anything that isn't genuinely better.

Receipts, not vibes. Early — feedback welcome.

video_script_scenes: I built a tool that uses AI to redesign a website — and then it taught me something about itself. To score a design's looks, it had an AI judge. And that judge had a blind spot.

Its original judge rated six things: hierarchy, spacing, alignment — all about legibility. But here's the catch: a page can be perfectly legible and still be empty. So the judge gave a nearly-blank draft its highest score — above a clean, finished page. It was rewarding nothing.

So I rebuilt the judge. Eleven dimensions now, and five of them are structural — depth, rhythm, contrast, distinctiveness. The scoring uses a band that peaks in the middle: you can't top it out by being empty, and you can't top it out by being cluttered. Real, composed design is what scores high.

Then I checked the fix honestly. I ran the new judge blind — six real screenshots, no labels, no hints about which was good. It scored my old generic site a four-point-eight, and three new redesigns a seven-point-seven. And it sorted all six into the right buckets. Six for six.
Same résumé, same ruler: before, four-point-eight. After, seven-point-seven. Three different redesigns — editorial, terminal, and Swiss — all proven better, not just different-looking.

It's open source — a Claude Code skill. It checks every change with hard metrics and a vision-judge, and it throws away anything that isn't actually better. Receipts, not vibes. It's early, so feedback is welcome. Find it at github dot com slash ziyilam three-nine-nine-nine slash ui dash evolve.
